Home / Website foundry

Enterprise build direction

From a business name to a governed website build.

A proposed foundry journey combines an HTML runtime template, customer administration, permitted storage and a versioned publishing path. The website foundry is a product direction; this portfolio does not claim those hosted adapters are already active.

1. Start with the business

Ask for the business name, sector and intended customer action. Keep the full business name visible in the title and content, even when its network address needs a shorter or encoded label.

2. Select a bounded template

A sector template should include page structure, attributed claims, accessible interactions and a customer/admin boundary. Domain-specific assertions require authoritative sources and appropriate review, rather than generic generated promises.

3. Choose a registration or namespace route

Customers can request registration of a desired public domain, or choose the owner-operated namespace and authoritative server service. VisitUsAt.<full-business-name>, TellMeAbout.<name>, WhatIs.<name> and WhoIs.<name> are proposed namespace patterns. The customer name remains visible in full; an explicit encoding contract handles spaces, punctuation and international characters. Resolver configuration and discovery determine which clients can resolve an independently operated namespace. Operating it does not by itself place its names in the public DNS root.

4. Serve with authenticated encryption

Both delivery routes can be designed for full HTTPS. Registered domains can use publicly trusted certificates; an independent namespace can use its own certificate authority with trust provisioned to participating clients. Certificate issuance, name validation, renewal and revocation are separate operational responsibilities. The reviewed runtime includes a TLS adapter; no public certificate issuance or native publication is claimed here.

4. Connect identity and storage

Google sign-in establishes an identity; it does not automatically grant Drive access. A customer must separately consent to the scoped Drive integration. A VFS adapter must map permitted files, handle revoked access and keep tokens outside the browser and public source.

5. Keep the admin workspace separate

Administrators need authenticated membership checks, project-scoped permissions and an audit record. Signing in is not enough to grant tenant administration or access to another customer’s files.

6. Compose nodes and lineage

Additional nodes need admitted identities, resource bounds and observed health. Mesh lineage should bind exact source and target generations. Node count alone does not prove resilience or independent failure domains.

7. Bound cache and cookie state

Active cache banks need per-customer keys, byte quotas, expiry and eviction rules. Authentication cookies need appropriate security attributes and logout behaviour. Private data must not enter shared public caches.

8. Publish and read back

A release needs a complete source identity, build and interaction checks, an authorised actuator, domain/TLS binding and a live readback. Faster delivery is a design objective, not a measured performance claim here.

A useful first evaluation

Choose one sector and one end-to-end customer journey. Define template inputs, storage consent, admin roles, an address under a controlled domain and observable publication acceptance before adding more tenants.

Resource grid and physical RAM target

The owner requests 100 TB of physical RAM per server, with each service receiving a governed VFS allocation inside the grid. This is a physical-capacity requirement, not a virtual address-space allocation. A segmented VFS can expose large extents through small 32-bit process windows. Server capacity, quotas and failure recovery must be measured separately; no 100 TB host has been provisioned by this portfolio build.

Failover across DNS and the service grid

Common service templates can define admitted identities, resource bounds, fresh health observations, committed generations and failover rules across DNS, namespace, VFS and website services. RAM-backed replication can support continuity while qualified replicas remain available. Recovery after loss of all replicas requires a separately demonstrated mechanism. TOT and 0.297 resonance are owner-specified protocol topics awaiting their authoritative specification and failure-case qualification.
